attacks.claim: The public Recent signers panel renders each signer's full name and full postal code, contradicting the agreed rule (first name, last initial, city only) and the proposal's own description. Public disclosure of PII to anonymous, CDN-cached, crawlable pages cannot be recalled; QA marked the panel Pass without any masking check.

The organizer-updates checkbox is pre-checked, so consent is not an affirmative act. This is invalid GDPR consent for EU signers, and it also contradicts the claim that signers 'can choose' to receive updates. Opted-in rows feed the organizer CSV export.

No GDPR rights handling is described for confirmed signers: no privacy notice or lawful basis, retention period, erasure or withdrawal path, or unsubscribe for organizer updates. The organizer-as-separate-controller relationship for CSV exports is also undocumented.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention period, erasure/withdrawal flow, unsubscribe, lawful basis for confirmed signatures; only unconfirmed signatures are purged after 7 days

attacks.claim: The submit handler only handles 422 and ok. A 409 duplicate or a 5xx gives no feedback, and the aria-live .form-error is never populated. Validation errors are shown only by color, with no text, which fails WCAG 2.1 AA error identification and use of color. Also, fetch follows redirects, so the Location header is likely unreadable and the post-sign redirect may break.
attacks.evidence: if (res.status === 422) {...return;} if (res.ok) window.location = res.headers.get('Location');

attacks.claim: The agreed WCAG 2.1 AA requirement is supported only by an automated axe scan of the default sign page. The Recent signers panel, error and duplicate states, and manual keyboard or screen-reader testing are not covered.
attacks.evidence: | axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations |

attacks.claim: The public sign endpoint has no described rate limit, bot protection, or CSRF handling. Each submission triggers a Postmark email, so a bot can drive email spend and spam third parties' addresses. The 409 duplicate response also allows probing which emails signed.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: rate limiting or bot protection on POST /p/{{ petition.slug }}/sign; only the export is described as rate-limited

attacks.claim: Signatures depend on Postmark confirmation emails, but there is no retry, failure handling, or resend path, and the 7-day purge then silently drops them. The user is shown no 'check your email' state. Rollout metrics (error rate, bounce rate) do not measure confirmation conversion, so silent signature loss would go unnoticed.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retry/resend path and post-submit pending-confirmation copy; "Watch `sign_submit_error_rate` (< 0.5%) and confirmation email bounce rate (< 2%) for 24h."

attacks.claim: Rollback only swaps the sign form for the Follow button. It does not say whether the Recent signers panel is behind the flag, nor how already-collected signatures, pending confirmations, or opted-in exports are handled. It is also untested in QA.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: flip `petitions_signing` off; sign form is replaced by the existing "Follow this petition" button.

attacks.claim: Load evidence covers only the sign POST rate. Count polling every 15s with a 10s CDN cache, the per-render recent_signers query, and the purge job and CSV export at volume are not tested or bounded.
attacks.evidence: Load: 400 signatures/s sustained for 10 min, p95 210ms | Pass

attacks.claim: Duplicate detection by email alone means an unconfirmed record, possibly created by someone else, blocks the real owner with a 409 until the purge. No re-request path is specified.
attacks.evidence: Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409 | Pass
